result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.set_edge_attrs_ws()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Set attributes on all selected edges. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L9304-L9386){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.set_edge_attrs_ws(**attributes) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Set attributes on selected edges](/assets/graphs/set-edge-attrs-ws.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Every edge carries a value w. Edges B–C, B–E, and D–E are selected in the accent color with values 1, 4, and 2; after the call all three read 5, while the other four edges keep their values." width="100%"} Updates or adds attributes to edges in the current selection. The `weight` attribute receives special handling as it's a first-class edge property. Requires an active edge selection. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [**attributes]{.doc-parameter-name} : Attribute name-value pairs to set on selected edges. Use `weight` to update edge weights directly. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} `weight` gets special handling since it's a first-class edge property rather than a generic attribute, but it's set the same way as any other keyword: ::: {#8b7bcb56 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_path_graph(3) edge_ids = graph.get_edge_ids() ( graph .select_edges_by_id([edge_ids[0]]) .set_edge_attrs_ws(weight=5.0, type='strong') ) edge = graph.get_edge(edge_ids[0]) edge.weight ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 5.0 ``` ::: ::: The custom `type` attribute lives alongside `weight` in `attributes`: ::: {#c9e1d7aa .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} edge.attributes['type'] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 'strong' ``` ::: ::: Selecting every edge first (`lambda e: True`) is a quick way to apply the same attribute graph-wide: ::: {#b489722c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(3) ( graph .select_edges(lambda e: True) .set_edge_attrs_ws(weight=1.0) ) graph.get_edge_attrs("weight") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {1: 1.0, 2: 1.0} ``` ::: :::
